body:
**Status: filed only.** This behaviour is shared with the CPU path (inherited from RELION `ad0b230`). Do not fix or merge a change until the maintainer decides; a fix changes CPU output and breaks RELION parity.

**Problem.** The correlation maps that both backends build for global and patch alignment carry a large constant offset (about 36000), while the peak contrast that decides the shift is about 1. Float32 resolves only about 0.004 at that magnitude, so the peak neighbourhood is stored coarsely rounded on both CPU and CUDA. Near-tied peaks are then ordered by rounding noise, and the iterative alignment, patch acceptance and polynomial fit amplify the different choice.

**Evidence** (PR #261, `docs/post_rc0/s1/peakfit_attribution/`; 10216, 12963 and Falcon 3 × 10 movies × 5×5/3×3 = 60 configurations; 4GPUs, Release builds):

| Diagnostic: CCF spectrum DC bin zeroed before the CCF inverse | S1-positive / 60 | Median max global gap |
|---|---:|---:|
| Neither backend (#254 only) | 17 | 0.039 px |
| CUDA only, against the original CPU | 16 | 0.054 px |
| CPU and CUDA | **0** (McNemar p = 1.9e-6) | **5.6e-6 px** |

- With both backends conditioned, product relative RMSE is about 4e-4 (median).
- Zeroing the DC term on the CPU alone moves CPU products by up to 0.59 relative RMSE. So on these families the existing CPU local-alignment result is itself decided by float rounding, not only the CUDA result.
- Zeroing the DC bin subtracts a constant from the map: in exact arithmetic it leaves peak positions and curvature unchanged.
- It also removes the cancellation in the peak-fit denominator (#257), which mostly comes from this offset.

**Mechanism location.** The CCF is formed in Fourier space and inverted to float: [CPU](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/blob/6d68e2d6/src/motioncorr_runner.cpp#L4761-L4772), [CUDA computeReferenceKernel/computeCCFKernel](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/blob/6d68e2d6/src/acc/cuda/cuda_alignpatch.cu#L130-L179). Neither removes the DC term.

**Not yet measured:**
- whether conditioning improves accuracy against known motion, as opposed to only CPU/CUDA agreement;
- the effect on the tutorial and the S1-negative families;
- the downstream comparison (S1.4, #238);
- the cost, expected to be negligible.

Related: #238, #257, #260, #256 §B.

## Next bounded experiment: validate conditioning against mathematics and motion truth

The latest maintainer direction is to prioritise correct motion correction over matching legacy CPU output. The #261 result supports making this the next numerical-validation target, but **0/60 CPU/CUDA disagreement-screen positives is not an accuracy result**. In particular, e10216-01 still fails the global iteration criterion on both conditioned paths while their images agree closely. Keep that shared failure visible.

### 1. Specify the operation and isolate it

For the existing circular Fourier CCF, replacing **only its spectrum's (0,0) bin** with zero changes the exact map by a spatial constant. Integer maximisers and quadratic curvature are therefore unchanged in exact arithmetic. The intended improvement is retaining contrast before float32 map storage. It is not a new motion model, whitening scheme or removal of the mean from the published micrograph.

Keep #254's input repair and #260's scalar fit fixed. Test four independently controlled arms: no CCF conditioning, global only, local only, both. Exercise CPU and CUDA as implementations of the same declared operation, each against independent references; do not choose the winner by similarity to the old CPU. Preserve tie rules, search bounds, convergence and fitting policy initially so their effects remain separable. Include both CCF execution paths and retries.

### 2. Stage-level acceptance independent of either backend

- Build small analytic CCFs or full-complex/direct-DFT high-precision references with known peaks/curvature. Vary the spectral DC pedestal while leaving non-DC coefficients identical. Compare the reconstructed zero-mean map and selected shifts against the defined reference.
- Measure absolute error and error relative to local peak contrast/curvature. Raw ULP counts across a large-pedestal and zero-mean map are not directly comparable.
- Test positive amplitude scaling away from the absolute guard threshold and overflow/subnormal limits. For stage-level offset tests, inject the offset after detector preprocessing, so hot-pixel thresholds or gain transformations do not confound the property.
- Cover flat/no-signal maps, exact and near ties, unbracketed boundary peaks, finite/nonfinite inputs and the current guard. A stable but arbitrary answer on a flat map is not evidence of measured motion.
- Confirm original/resident movie spectra, reconstruction brightness/DC and dose weighting are unchanged directly by this CCF-only operation. Validate actual C2R input conjugacy under the specified geometry independently.

A high-precision *calculation of the same CCF* is a numerical reference, not a ground-truth motion oracle. Keep those questions distinct.

### 3. Motion-truth acceptance

Extend the existing analytic-Gaussian known-motion generator rather than replacing it. Add controlled pedestal/contrast sweeps, many independent low-SNR seeds, abrupt early drift, long/large and nonsquare geometries, frame grouping and valid binning settings. Use an independent continuous-image generator or oversampled synthesis, not the production shift/crop helper. Separate motions representable by the existing polynomial from deliberately out-of-model fields.

Primary outputs: true global/local/applied-field vector errors in pixels and Å (RMS, tails, maxima, time dependence), residual transfer of known signal, convergence/ambiguity rates and correct handling of unidentifiable motion. Retain border and constant-origin accounting separately; do not re-register per frame until errors disappear. Use full-precision native coefficients for estimator checks and a separate STAR round-trip test (#265).

The current noisy truth fixture's accuracy failure is characterization, despite the launcher's OVERALL PASS. It should be explicitly included in the new accuracy assessment. Frozen fixtures and historical verdicts stay intact; new fixtures/seeds and criteria are declared prospectively.

### 4. Real-data qualification

Keep all existing census rows as development/regression evidence, including newly worse and shared-nonconverged cases. Test held-out movies/collections before selecting a production default, then #61's prospective CTF/particle/FSC/B-factor protocol. Cluster uncertainty by movie/collection rather than treating two grids or millions of pixels as independent experiments.

An intentional, justified change to inherited CPU output is a compatibility change to document, **not a scientific reason to retain a numerical defect**. This comment proposes the bounded validation work; it does not merge code, relax existing thresholds, or assert that conditioning has already improved downstream science. See the updated reviews on #254, #260 and #261.

Diagnostic handoff: `diag/s1-dc-oracle`, native source `afba50a4cebf5238ec2d267ff3ec07d272b13395` (tooling head `95e9d913`); Release CPU/CUDA builds and default-off byte controls pass; all 600 census runs completed, fixed-input double DC neutrality ≤1.71e-10 px; complete evidence is PR #271, with whole-pipeline float-feedback sensitivity and e10216-01 global nonconvergence retained.

title: CCF DC pedestal makes local alignment depend on float rounding on both CPU and CUDA (S1 driver)
